rules.specification: The checker needs the selected dictionary and edition, together with any approved spelling exceptions. The page does not define what evidence is sufficient to establish a user need.
rules.violation_condition: A later-listed spelling variant is used instead of the selected dictionary’s first-listed spelling, without evidence that the alternative meets a user need.
when: Applies where the selected dictionary lists alternative spellings of the same word.
An alternative listed spelling is permitted where there is evidence that it meets a user need.

Specific Style Manual guidance for a term or phrase takes precedence over the dictionary default.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the user-need exception and dictionary-dependent variations qualify one spelling-choice check rather than creating additional rules.

rules.quote: Record decisions you make about alternative spellings in a style sheet.
rules.violation_condition: A decision to use an alternative dictionary spelling in the associated content is missing from its style sheet.
when: Applies when an alternative spelling listed in the selected dictionary has been chosen.
Assess the style sheet against the spelling decisions made for the associated content.
rules.why: The missing record is a distinct textual omission, not the spelling-choice violation itself.

rules.why: This specifies a property of the style sheet, unlike the adjacent advice about consulting specialist dictionaries.

rules.quote: The important thing is to use the word that matches the meaning you want to convey.
